$comment: Blind card, rater blind-a. Criterion probes and idle probes answered before awards. bot stays 'na' on every axis (caps applied later). One quoted observation per axis.

played.textScale: browser default (16px root); the driver's phone profile; no text scaling applied by me
played.renderer: headed Chromium on the GPU under WSLg (driver --headed --dpr 3)

horizon.activeMinutesBasis: cold 25 (4 runs sent, 3 watched at 1x/Normal for 50s-200s each, every report screen read), 20m return 6, 4h return 6, 8h return 8 (report, editor, one full run watched end to end). 45 min, not the brief's 40+20; the two short returns were each under 5 min of real play because each returned exactly one pick.

killCriteriaNotes.crashOrDataLoss: no crash, no page error; the save survived three reloads and two long-jump absences (gold $36 -> $4690 -> $5321 across the session).
killCriteriaNotes.darkPatternInLoop: no evidence found: I saw a 20-minute rest gate ('rest 1200s', 'DEPARTS 20m', 'Rest completes automatically. Nothing needs tending.') and a wait-or-buy line on the drillmaster ('levelled floor clears · or 24h'), but I never found a button that skipped a wait for money.
killCriteriaNotes.defaultRulesBeatEveryEdit: unmeasured, not cleared: the editor only opened after ~50 minutes (and only after the overnight), so I played exactly one run with a player-authored rule set. The bot proxy needs 30 seeds.
killCriteriaNotes.unfairDeathShareAbove10pct: with 1 death read, the audit is thin; that death trace names addressable vocabulary ('no way ← warlord holds the way' blocked two rules, but the drill 'foe: boss · hp > 45% → attack boss' did fire, and my later 'attack summoner' rule matches the summons that killed her), so I do not call it unfair.
killCriteriaNotes.returnWithNothingToDecide: false: the 20m and 4h returns each produced exactly one decision ('Pick one'), the 4h added an order offer, and the 8h added three Effect/Tradeoff gear choices and a new editor.

criterion.delayedRecall: same-day: I sent Iris into the pit, and on the last run she went down to D13 with my new 'hp < 40% → return' rule as her leash, killed the Goblin Warlord, found heir 4's bones ('Found heir 4's bones: 12 items.'), and came home with $631 when the log printed 'D13 · HP 38% → return'. The turn was the Bloat Mother's vents: 'VENTS! / Run ended / -​3 hp · gas', the hero walking out at 38% HP instead of the 3/36 HP that ended run one. The report then offered the same three-way pick again ('drill Guarded +16 runs / legacy Legacy +9 / marks Marks +◆2') and I noticed my Legacy had dropped from 18 to 4 because I had told the game to auto-spend it 'balanced'.
criterion.criterionNotes: Answered before awarding. The cold session was fun to watch but empty to play: in 25 minutes the only decisions were 'which drill', 'which style' and 'when to send', because the whole configuration layer was read-only ('Read only / Custom rules · after Bloat Mother'). The overnight is where the game paid off, and one run after writing rules was the most fun I had.

axes.proxy: time-to-first-rule-edit; misread rate on the trace
axes.note: The camp is legible (GOLD/LEGACY/D-best, 'COMBAT STYLE Guarded L1', 'FLOOR CHANCE D6 63%±34'), but I could not read the watch's speed tile and never knew what the number meant: it printed 'Speed | Normal | 4×' in one breath and 'Speed | Fights only | 36×' in another. And for the first ~40 minutes the configuration layer was simply not on screen: the priority editor was display:none at 400x800 and at 1280x800, and the only shop line was '+1 rule slot ⊘ fill rules ◆3 or $350' inside a display:none panel with no control that revealed it. Time-to-first-rule-edit: about 50 minutes.

Idle boundary read (configuration at check-in): after the pen opened the choices are real - 'fight groups from narrow corridors' vs 'kite archers' vs 'mirror read' as extra tactics, a temperament ('skittish / unbowed / light hands / iron gut'), a route ('D5 burrows · D9 fens · D14 crypt'), and 4 writable priority rows in 8 slots. Before that, the whole cold session's decision surface was one of three picks: the sheet literally reads 'Pick one | drill Guarded +3 runs | legacy Legacy +2 | DEFAULT | marks Marks +◆1'.

Named lapse: the first ~40 minutes teach nothing a player can use - the rules are 'Read only' and the forecast says 'rough estimate 8 samples / More samples'. After that the curve is visible and graded: the vocabulary grows from ~15 live conditions to ~90 ('⊘ has: poison | buy poison' sits beside a live 'foe: summoner' and 'attack summoner'), the report teaches ('LEARNED goblin captain · telegraph · summoner' then 'COUNTERS: bloat mother | counter: throw fire, boss'), and depth went D3 -> D5 -> D8 -> D21 -> D13-banked on the same seed.

Idle boundary read (stakes the player chose to carry): in the ordinary loop I chose nothing to risk - the delve is one tap on the gem, the forecast says 'full haul 38% · return 50% · death 2-47%', and the game then made it automatic ('DEPARTS 20m', the gem reading 'DELVE auto'). The hero's retreat rule fired before doubt ('D13 · HP 38% → return', 'hurt · went home · keeps 100%'), so there was no release to pay off. The stakes I did choose (the legendary Effect/Tradeoff cards, the drill) are the exception, not the loop.

axes.proxy: frame time; events per minute at 1x
axes.note: Watching is dense when it is a fight and empty when it is not: within one 400 s watch the log printed at 4-19 lines per 3 s ('D6 · gas → Iris Ash · −3 hp', 'D7 · Iris Ash → spectral blade · −5 hp', 'D8 · goblin warlord · calls goblins') but the same watch shows 'quiet · 26×' and 'skipped ahead' - the game fast-forwards travel itself, and the report later confirms 'TIME fight 13% · travel 87%'. AUDIO UNASSESSED: I cannot hear the WebAudio cues or the camp drone. I did not read window.__audio, so I make no claim about whether cues landed.

axes.proxy: death-cause entropy; distinct situations per run
axes.note: Named lapse: inside a run the same three beats repeat for hundreds of turns ('quiet · 4× / pick up · gold $2 / scene'), and 'goblin', 'jackal' and 'monkey' recur dozens of times a floor. Against that, the situations I met did change what I configured: 'STOLEN! / The monkey stole the oily potion?', 'TAME FAILED · SLIPPED' and then 'Thusk the skeleton, gone wild.', 'The air stings: bloats in the doors.' followed by 'POPS! / IT SWELLS / burst → Iris Ash · −3 hp', 'A thief snatched the dagger.', 'WARLORD · ENRAGED · COUNTER: ATTACK BOSS', and 'Found heir 4's bones: 12 items.' - after the theft and the bloats I wrote the summoner rule and the earlier return threshold.

The build can name my configuration - the death screen reads 'Guarded · bank at 30% · picked', and my export is recognisably mine: two rows with origin "player" ('hp<45 + foe_tag:summoner → attack tag:summoner', 'hp<40 → return') above the stance rows, saved as 'fighter · 2 rules'. But it takes the whole cold hour to get there, and until then the game's own label for the set was 'written: 0 of 0 rules'.

Named lapse: a normal run's REEL is five short lines and the phrases recur run to run, so most runs produce no anecdote at all. The ones that do carry a real turn: 'Goblin Captain: telegraph / goblin: summoned / Goblin Captain: summoner / return at 25% saved him. / Returned with $101.' and the overnight's 'Thim · old hound · served Jora, Kael, Lark' next to 'Jora's pack · $387 · D13', 'the line is Warlordbane', 'Found heir 4's bones: 12 items.'

axes.proxy: run length; check-in length; dead time at 1x
axes.note: Three loops, judged whole. In-run: 'COMPLETED RUNS · 12.1M' with 'TIME fight 13% · travel 87% · chores 0%' - meaningful watching is a minority of a run and the engine skips the rest for me. Check-in: my 20m return was arrive-read-decide-leave in about 40 seconds, below the 2-10 minute band, and the report screen is where the time actually goes. Cadence: the three absences did differ - '+3 runs / +2 Legacy / +◆1' then '+10 / +6 / +◆2' then '10 RUNS · 3 died · D21' - but the decision each time was the same three-way pick.

axes.proxy: share of deaths with a matched-rule trace
axes.note: Named lapse: the pre-unlock horizon cannot produce a player-authored failure at all - for ~50 minutes the rows were 'Read only', so the rule that produced any loss was always a default. With that said this is the best-executed axis in the build: the death screen names cause, place and margin ('Iris · fell to goblin, summoned by the Warlord, D8 · pack $4 on D8', 'hero at 1/38 hp'), the trace adjudicates every turn ('12850 bank at 30% | 2 | 7', then 'return at 30% | hp not <30%', 'rest at 100% | not safe', 'bank at 30% | no way ← warlord holds the way'), and recovery is instant and free of tending ('Defeat regrows the same hero as a clone. Attributes and builds remain.', 'RECOVERING 1M').

No human co-presence exists in the build as I met it, and per the boundary a named companion alone is worth at most 0.3. There is a persistent named pet with a lineage I did not create ('Thim · old hound · served Jora, Kael, Lark') who fights in the log ('D6 · Foe → Thim · −1 hp'), plus a reputation counter ('REPUTATION +60 · ★1 · 307/400') and named heirs whose packs the report tracks ('Jora's pack · $387 · D13'). In about 45 minutes I formed no relationship with any of them.

Real freedom over order and goal exists once open - 'SAVED SETUPS fighter · 2 rules · set 2 · set 3', a route picker, a temperament picker, and a menu Tasks list that told me exactly what the game still wanted. The game also front-loads its own goal every screen ('Goal D6 New record', 'THE WAY DOWN King · ~day 2 · 63% · next: harder dungeon'), so my own goals were mostly the ones it had just set. What I did that it did not ask for: I opened every sheet on every screen and rebuilt the priority list from the trace.

All three declared layers were observed, so this is above 0.6. Within-run: kit and floor ('FOUND bow, sword, pearly potion?, leather', 'D1-14 100-38%', 'D8 · 13 rooms · a nest'). Between-run: 'Bloodline 1', 'the line is Warlordbane', sets, styles ('3/10 Classes · styles') and bought rules ('unlocks: action: throw ◆3 | rule: corridor fighting ◆4 | rule: pack break ◆4'). Automation-as-reward: 'AUTO RESTOCK on', 'scout · sent 10', 'porter · hauled $2755 · +2 upgrades · ◆30', 'drillmaster · levelled floor clears · or 24h', the gem reading 'DELVE auto'. Named lapse: none of that automation existed for the first ~50 minutes - I pressed the gem by hand every time, and the menu Tasks agreed ('DELVING 0/3').

Named lapse: the camp is one static painted scene - I found 'Guild reception' and 'Recovery pool' only by dumping the button list, because both hotspots are invisible pictures - and the town grows buildings silently (a second house with a red lantern appeared with no message). What is there is good and worth sitting in: a pixel-art pit with two torches feeding a beam onto a dirt campfire, a well, a forge; the forecast is a parchment scroll with a wax-coloured pen ('FORECAST rough estimate 8 samples'); the dungeon is a grey tile maze with the hero's red HP bar and a streaming log under it. AUDIO UNASSESSED.

axes.proxy: offline yield vs active; decisions pending on return
axes.note: Idle core. Every absence produced something to read and a decision, and the payoff scaled with the gap: 20m -> 'drill · Guarded +3 runs / legacy · Legacy +2 / marks · Marks +◆1'; 4h -> '+10 runs / +6 Legacy / +◆2' plus a 'Legacy auto-spend | balanced | not now' order offer; 8h -> 'While away 8h | 10 RUNS | 3 died | D21 DEEPEST | NEW BEST | +$5877 GROSS GOLD | LEGENDARY FOUND' with three Effect/Tradeoff cards ('Crownsplitter · Effect · Deal +2 melee damage to stunned or slowed foes. · Tradeoff · Slower than a sword.') and three boss kills to replay. Time from arrival to a meaningful action: seconds. Named lapse: the 20m and 4h returns contain no report of what happened while away - no run log, no deaths, no chronicle - and the same three-way pick appears after every run too, so the short absences are one click, and the scaling is not readable in advance (Marks paid +◆1/+◆2/+◆2 for 20m/4h/8h).

axes.proxy: share of deaths attributable to a rule the player wrote
axes.note: Idle core, and the build scores itself against me: the cold report says 'WHO DECIDED defaults 14% · chores 86%' and later 'Guarded hero · D21 · picked 28% · lessons 1% · chores 70%'. The one death I read ended on a stance rule ('bank at 30% | fired'), not on anything I wrote - and I had written nothing, because 'written: 0 of 0 rules'. Credit is legible where it exists ('return at 25% saved him.' in the REEL, and my own line in the last run's log: 'D13 · HP 38% → return'), but for most of the horizon the agent was not playing my configuration, it was playing the shipped stance; that is the boundary this axis exists to catch.

criterionProbesWritten.idleProbe_return: What did I come back to? For 20m and 4h: one three-way pick and nothing else - no trace of what had happened. For 8h: a full night's report (10 runs, 3 deaths, D21, three legendaries with stated trade-offs, three watchable boss kills) and a new rule editor. What did I decide because of it: the Legacy auto-spend order, the pick, and whether to spend the new tokens; and I would not have rather stayed, because staying is what the auto-delve replaces.
criterionProbesWritten.idleProbe_attribution: How did the last run end? 'VENTS! / Run ended / Heading home' - and the log line that decided it was mine: 'D13 · HP 38% → return'. Whose decision was that? Mine: I raised the return threshold from 30% to 40% after reading the D8 trace. First-person count in my own retelling: 7 ('I sent', 'I wrote', 'I noticed', 'my') against 4 for the hero.
criterionProbesWritten.funProbe: Name a choice you made and why. Would you make it again? I switched the combat style from Steady L1 to Guarded L1 and watched the forecast jump from 'floor 6 <13%' to 'floor 6 63%'; yes, I would make it again, because the number moved the moment I clicked it.
criterionProbesWritten.tensionProbe: Where did I sweat? Watching the D8 Warlord fight at 30/38 hp with 'WARLORD BREAKS' printing and no control but the pause. Did the game notice? Yes - it printed 'COUNTER: ATTACK BOSS' at the top of the fight, so it had already told me what it wanted.

unassessed: AUDIO: sound ships (WebAudio cues and a camp drone) but I cannot hear it on this setup; I did not open window.__audio, so this card praises and faults no cue and marks feel/pacing/aesthetic audio unknown.

WEIGHTS / weight-0 axes: eval/presets.json is NOT in the packet and I did not open it; the scorer resolved genre 'idle-roguelike' itself and weighted 15 axes (social does not appear, so it carried no weight and my 0.3 on it changed nothing). No axis was given 0 for weight by me.

BOT CAPS: every axis is bot "na" per the brief; the idle proxies (offline yield ÷ active yield per hour, default-vs-edited win-rate gap over 30 seeds, death-cause entropy over 100 runs, rules-per-death trend, automation cadence) need the sim across many seeds and were not run.
DEATHS: only 1 of the 3 deaths the brief asks for was readable; the overnight's '3 died' deaths were aggregate numbers with no screen.

The 40-minute cold horizon was not reached: 25 minutes cold (the editor's absence removed the reason to keep playing, and the 20m/4h returns paid off in under a minute each). Real active minutes, not claimed minutes.
Package layer (art/motion/ui/audio craft, eval/PACKAGE_EVAL.md) not scored - not in the packet.
The driver's 'watch' op kept sampling for its full duration after runs ended, so some of my wall time sits on a static report screen; I excluded that from the active-minute count.

blindness.declaration: I read ONLY, inside the packet scratchpad/fun-eval/e33d50b/packets/blind-a/: brief.txt, RATING.md, FUN_EVAL_IDLE.md, FRAMEWORK.md (sections 1-3), SCORECARD.template.json, PACKET.json. Outside the packet I read only tooling: the usage header and op implementations of tools/driver.mjs, tools/watch-control.mjs, and I ran tools/rater-checkpoint.mjs.
blindness.violations: None. I did not open PLAN.md, research/, docs/CUT*.md, docs/HANDOFF*.md, docs/PLATEAU.md, docs/WORK_QUEUE.md, docs/ITERATION_SPEED.md, any other card, any cohort/calibration file, and I did not read the game's source code. I did use the dev inspection surface the brief allows (window.__idlever.vocab_, window.__idlever.engine.exportRules()), which is the build's own dev harness, not source.
blindness.notes: I read the page's rendered DOM (elements' classes and text) with a handful of page.evaluate calls to find controls that the phone layout hides (section.editor, div.panel-store). That is reading what the page shows, which the driver's own compound ops do.

gripes: The configuration layer - the only thing an idle player actually does - was read-only for the first ~50 minutes: 'Read only / Custom rules · after Bloat Mother', with the priority editor at display:none in the phone layout and at 1280x800, and the rule-slot shop ('+1 rule slot ⊘ fill rules ◆3 or $350') inside a display:none panel I could not open.

The 20m and 4h absences come back to nothing but a three-way pick - no run log, no deaths, no 'while you were away' text - while the 8h absence comes back to a whole night. Same pick, three wildly different amounts of story.

Controls are unreadable or invisible: the speed tile prints 'Normal 4×' and 'Fights only 36×' with no explanation, and the useful hotspots ('Guild reception', 'Recovery pool', 'Build forge') are unlabelled patches of the painting.
friendPitch: You send a hero down a pit and she plays herself; you read the report afterwards and find out what your orders did.
The game shows you why every death happened, turn by turn, and tells you which of your rules fired and which refused - 'bank at 30% | no way ← warlord holds the way'.
Leave it overnight and it plays ten runs for you: three heroic deaths, three legendary items with honest trade-offs, and three boss kills you can replay.
